findings.title: The corrected split_at_word_edges docstring overstates what removing the cut would affect, and reads a font-wide fact as if it were measured on the 34
findings.claim_or_code: "...they were up to 0.99 pt per segment on the 34, and not only short: Liberation's r'/f' pairs draw longer. The cut is kept as it was; removing it would re-segment every translated label."
findings.evidence: compose.py:219-227 `line_segments` calls FS.split_at_word_edges only `if any(st is not None for _, st in segs)`, so a line with no styled segment never reaches the cut. figscripts.py:452-469 cuts only a plain segment next to a styled one. Recount over evidence/2026-09-17-c6b-build/reports/before/items/*.items.json (34 figures): 176 layout blocks; only 34 have any line with more than one segment; 12 have two adjacent same-size, same-weight, same-slant segments on one baseline, which is the cut's signature. The 'not only short' clause sits next to 'on the 34', but the census (before/census.json, recounted from the raw items) has layout short 27, long 0. Widening pairs exist in the font, not on the 34.
findings.consequence: A later session deciding whether to drop the cut (its stated reasons, rounding and kerning, are now both neutralised) would take on a false blast radius: re-segmenting every translated label, so re-reviewing all 31 recomposed figures. The measured exposure is at most 34 of 176 blocks, and the cut fires on about 12. This is the 'stale premise in a comment' class the repo's CLAUDE.md warns about, added in the same commit that corrected the previous premise.
findings.suggested_fix: Say 'removing it would re-segment every translated line that holds a styled (formula/script/italic) segment next to a space' (optionally: 12 of 176 layout blocks on the 34). Separate the font fact from the measurement, e.g. '0 long on the 34, but Liberation's f’/r’ pairs would draw longer'.

At lines 224-226 it runs only `if any(st is not None for _, st in segs)`, and that function's own docstring says "only when a style is present". The cut itself cuts only a plain segment that sits next to a styled one and has a space inside it. So a translated line with no styled segment never reaches the cut, and removing the cut would not change it. The spec's own K3 says "would re-segment translated labels", without "every". The docstring added "every".

I recounted from reports/before/items/*.items.json (34 files, 370 layout items, which matches the census). There are 176 layout blocks, counting a block as a run opening at line 0, seg 0. 34 blocks have a line with more than one segment. 12 blocks, in 8 figures, carry the cut's signature: two neighbouring segments with the same size, weight and slant on one baseline. The docstring does say "Liberation's", which softens this half: it is ambiguous rather than flatly false. The "up to 0.99 pt" figure is correct (max_abs_resid_0 = 0.992).

This is not a duplicate. The spec review (review.json) only records that K3 names this docstring for correction. It does not flag this overstatement.

findings.title: Three new comments name the widening kern pairs with an ASCII apostrophe; the font kerns only U+2019
findings.claim_or_code: compose.py: "Liberation's r'/f' pairs are positive and would draw a segment LONGER than measured"; figscripts.py: "Liberation's r'/f' pairs draw longer"; svgout.py: "Liberation's r'/f' pairs would draw it LONGER" (all three bytes are U+0027, checked with od -c)
findings.evidence: Read-only fontTools probe of the four svgout.FACES files: kern[(r, U+0027)] = None and kern[(f, U+0027)] = None in Regular, Bold, Italic and BoldItalic. The positive Latin pairs are r+quoteright U+2019 (+76 in all four) and f+quoteright (+37; +76 in Italic). The decision record and spec write them correctly as `f’` / `r’`.
findings.consequence: Someone checking the comment, or planting a regression fixture for the 'draws LONGER' direction, with the pair as written (r' in ASCII) gets 0 kerning. They would conclude the premise behind the ruling's 'fails toward collision' argument is false, or build a control that cannot fire.
findings.suggested_fix: Write `r’`/`f’` (U+2019), or spell it out: 'r and f before a right single quotation mark (U+2019)'.

verdict.reasoning: I could not disprove it. I checked all three comments byte by byte. compose.py:191, figscripts.py:448 and svgout.py:116 each write `r'/f'`, and every quote mark is an ASCII apostrophe, U+0027. I then ran a read-only fontTools probe on the four files in svgout.FACES (LiberationSans Regular, Bold, Italic and BoldItalic under /usr/share/fonts/truetype/liberation/). In each face the apostrophe maps to the glyph `quotesingle`, and no face has a kern pair for r or f followed by `quotesingle`, in either the GPOS table or the legacy kern table. The widening Latin pairs all use `quoteright`, which is U+2019. So the comments name a character pair the fonts never kern. The design record (decision line 44) and the spec (line 33) write the pairs correctly as `f’`/`r’` with U+2019, so only the three code comments lost the character. Two things make it less serious without refuting it. The same comments write "Liberation's" with an ASCII apostrophe, so `r'` may simply be an ASCII stand-in rather than a factual error. And the files already contain non-ASCII characters (§, ⑥b), so writing the correct U+2019 costs nothing. One detail to add: BoldItalic has a third positive Latin pair, quoteright+t at +37. It does not change the finding.
verdict.evidence:
1. The comments, via `grep -an "r'/f'" svgout.py compose.py figscripts.py` piped to `od -c`, show `r ' / f '` with plain ASCII quote bytes at svgout.py:116, figscripts.py:448 and compose.py:191. The diff a62d51ab..HEAD shows all three lines are new in this branch.
2. The fonts (fontTools, reading both GPOS and kern) give these values:
   - Regular: r+’ is 76, f+’ is 37, and r+' and f+' have no entry.
   - Bold: the same as Regular.
   - Italic: r+’ is 76, f+’ is 76, and r+' and f+' have no entry.
   - BoldItalic: r+’ is 76, f+’ is 37, and r+' and f+' have no entry.
3. The apostrophe maps to the glyph `quotesingle` and U+2019 maps to `quoteright`. The only positive Latin pairs in GPOS are:
   - Regular and Bold: f+quoteright 37, r+quoteright 76.
   - Italic: f+quoteright 76, r+quoteright 76.
   - BoldItalic: f+quoteright 37, r+quoteright 76, and also quoteright+t 37.
4. The docs use U+2019: docs/decisions/2026-09-17-translated-figure-labels-drawn-unkerned.md:44 has "the Latin ones are `f’` and `r’`", and docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-17-c140-c6b-translated-labels-unkerned-design.md:33 has "`f’` (+37) and `r’` (+76) widen".
verdict.corrected_finding: The finding holds as reported (minor, documentation accuracy). The comments at compose.py:191, figscripts.py:448 and svgout.py:116 name the widening pairs as `r'/f'` using an ASCII apostrophe (U+0027). None of the four Liberation Sans faces kerns r or f before U+0027. The positive Latin GPOS pairs are r plus U+2019 (+76 in all four faces) and f plus U+2019 (+37, or +76 in Italic). BoldItalic also has U+2019 plus t at +37. The decision record and spec use U+2019 correctly. A regression fixture or spot-check that copies the comment literally gets zero kerning and cannot show the "draws LONGER" direction. The fix is to write `r’`/`f’` with U+2019, or to spell out "r/f before U+2019 RIGHT SINGLE QUOTATION MARK". The files are already UTF-8 and contain other non-ASCII characters.

precondition('K0 CONTROL ...', len(lab_els) >= 3 and len(kept_els) == 2 and len(lab_els) + len(kept_els) == len(els1), ...)

It skips exactly the elements is_kept_element marks as kept and adds every other element to the nearest of the three labels. A stray non-label, non-kept element (for example a run-exact element drawn off its source origin) is silently absorbed into a label, and it surfaces as a confusing K1 failure rather than at the 'partition' control the comment says guards it.
findings.suggested_fix: Drop the sum-equality clause, or relabel it as structural. Make the real control explicit, e.g. assert every lab_els element's text is drawn from the three translated values (the sentinel() helper already exists), so an element belonging to neither population can actually fail K0.
